deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page sits between the previous page and the next page, both about the profinite 'groupe à lacets' \hat\Pi_{0,3}. That is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, presented by l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1, together with its peripheral (inertia) structure. The previous page computes automorphisms that commute (up to inner automorphisms) with the S_3-symmetries ρ and σ_0. This page is a general 'functoriality' interlude. It asks how automorphisms of a loop group π that respect its loop structure (denoted 𝒯, i.e. the conjugacy classes of the peripheral subgroups / 'lacets') behave under a morphism φ: π → π'. Typically φ is a filling-in ('bouchage') of some punctures: π = π_1 of a surface with puncture set I, and π' = π_1 of the surface with only I' ⊂ I kept.

(1) Top diagram. Objects B_π, \tilde B_π, B_{π,Γ}, B_Γ, \tilde B_Γ, and a variant with a subgroup Γ_1 ⊂ Γ. They are arranged in a commutative ladder over φ: π → π'. The most plausible reading is classifying objects or automorphism-type groups:
- \tilde B ~ the group of automorphisms;
- B ~ the outer automorphisms, or the corresponding 'Teichmüller' modular object;
- B_{π,Γ} ~ the relative object for π together with an operation of a group Γ (e.g. a Galois or symmetry group such as the S_3 of the next page).
The arrows say these constructions are contravariantly or covariantly functorial in φ and in Γ_1 ⊂ Γ. The precise meaning of B is not determinable from the page alone.

(2) Descent of automorphisms along φ. Statement: given u ∈ Aut(π) compatible with 𝒯, there exists a unique u' ∈ Aut(π') compatible with 𝒯 with u'φ(g) = φ(u(g)) for all g, i.e. u'φ = φu. Uniqueness is automatic when φ is surjective. Existence holds exactly when u preserves Ker φ. That is automatic if Ker φ is the normal subgroup generated by the inertia of the filled-in punctures and u respects 𝒯 while fixing the set of filled punctures.
The scratch computations then pass to the outer version. If u is only given up to inner automorphisms, the compatibility becomes u'φ = int(g)·φu (written u'φu^{-1} = int(g)φ). He then begins defining the subgroup
𝓔_φ = {u ∈ Aut(π) | ∃ u' ∈ Aut(π') with u'φ = (int g)φu}
of automorphisms that descend.

(3) Bottom diagram: a morphism of extensions
1 → π → \hat S(π, I') → ...
1 → π' → \hat S(π') → \hat C(π') → 1
with vertical maps φ, f_π and f_{\hat S}. Here:
- \hat S(π') ⊂ Aut(π') is the group of 𝒯-compatible automorphisms;
- \hat C(π') ⊂ Out(π') is the group of 𝒯-compatible outer automorphisms;
- p is the projection, with kernel π' since π' is center-free.
- There is an isomorphism ψ_{I'}: \hat C(π, I') ≅ \hat S(π'), with the remark \hat S(π') ≃ \hat C(π, I').
This is the profinite, group-theoretic form of the Dehn–Nielsen–Baer plus Birman correspondence. Outer automorphisms of the group with one more puncture (fixing it) correspond to automorphisms of the group with that puncture filled. The row 1 → π' → \hat S(π') → \hat C(π') → 1 is a profinite Birman exact sequence, with π' acting by 'point pushing'.

Purpose: to build the 'Teichmüller tower' of profinite modular-type groups \hat C(π) and their compatibility with the bouchage maps. This is preparatory to describing the action of Gal(\bar Q/Q), or a candidate group like \hat{GT}, on the whole tower via its action on \hat\Pi_{0,3}.
errors: The isomorphism ψ_{I'}: \hat C(π,I') ≅ \hat S(π') is asserted without justification. For abstractly defined profinite groups of 𝒯-compatible automorphisms it is a nontrivial statement: a profinite analogue of Dehn–Nielsen–Baer/Birman. It is closely tied to congruence-subgroup-type questions; it was proved later, e.g. genus 0/1 work of Asada and related anabelian results of Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki.

Existence of u' requires u(Ker φ) = Ker φ. This holds only if u respects the specific peripheral classes being filled in, not merely 𝒯 globally. The page's 'compatible avec 𝒯' needs to include fixing (or permuting compatibly) the filled cusps. This is precisely why he is about to introduce the restricted subgroup 𝓔_φ.
The scratch equations contain crossed-out false starts (e.g. u'φu^{-1} = φ, u'φ = φu). The final version u'φ = int(g)φu is the correct outer-compatibility condition.

ideas.what: Descent of structure-preserving automorphisms along a fill-in map φ: π → π' and the subgroup 𝓔_φ of automorphisms that descend (up to inner)
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of Out^*(π) under puncture-forgetting maps; 'cusp-preserving' outer automorphisms compatible with fill-in
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for discrete groups (Birman 1969); profinite: Nakamura, Asada, Hoshi–Mochizuki (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), qualitatively (Teichmüller tower, bouchage/découpage operations)

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → π' → \hat S(π') → \hat C(π') → 1 with \hat S(π') ≅ \hat C(π, I') (π with one extra puncture)
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Birman exact sequence / profinite Dehn–Nielsen–Baer
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman (discrete); profinite versions Asada (2001), Nakamura, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme; not stated explicitly to my knowledge

ideas.what: Ladder of objects B_π, \tilde B_π, B_{π,Γ}, B_Γ functorial in φ and in subgroups Γ_1 ⊂ Γ
ideas.modern_name: Unclear: probably automorphism/outer-automorphism (or classifying) objects relative to a group Γ of symmetries

missed.claim: Explicit 1981 formulation, in purely profinite group-theoretic terms, of the Birman exact sequence for 𝒯-compatible automorphism groups of profinite loop groups, with \hat S(π') ≅ \hat C(π, I'). It is used as a building block for the profinite Teichmüller tower before Esquisse. This anticipates the 'combinatorial cuspidalization' theme later developed by Nakamura and Hoshi–Mochizuki. It is a historical precedence detail rather than new mathematics.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck took the profinite Birman/Dehn–Nielsen correspondence as a working axiom of the tower in 1981. The specific statement was only proved (in various genera) decades later.

deep.surprise_reason: Scratch-work page setting up standard functoriality of automorphism groups under fill-in maps and a profinite Birman sequence. It is historically interesting as an early profinite formulation, but the content is the expected background of the Teichmüller tower program, and later work covers it.
transcription_corrections: Bottom right vertical labels look like φ_π and φ_{\hat S} (curly φ) rather than f_π, f_{\hat S}.
The parenthetical '(≃ \hat C(π, I'))' annotates the bottom-row middle term \hat S(π'), restating the isomorphism ψ_{I'}.
Line under 'u' with a vertical bar: the second equation reads u'φ = int(g) φ(u), with 'φu' crossed out.
